content.comment_body: Request for help: I'm having trouble uploading a program to a new [article_no] standard module. I'm using the provided USB cable and [product_name] V[version_no]. I've tried lowering the transfer rate and ensuring the correct COM port and cable are selected, but the system won't connect. The device is powered on. Assistance appreciated. [user_name]
Hello, what error message appears when you try to upload the program to the controller? Have you tested other transfer rates? Best regards.
Unable to access IP address on COM25.
Please note, I'm new to programming and to [product_name], so I might be making a beginner's mistake.

Hi [user_name], Which version of [product_name] software are you using? What kind of cable is connected? Some USB-RS232 converters automatically select COM port numbers, so it's useful to verify the active port in Windows Device Manager. Was this information useful? w
Hello, I'm using V[version_no] software and the USB cable specific to [product_name].
Sorry [user_name], I haven't used that setup before, so can't offer direct assistance. (My setup is on [product_name] V[version_no]; I haven't switched to V[version_no] yet.)

I'm on version [version_no], even with an older [article_no]. For [product_name] RS232 connections, I use a USB to RS232 adapter. The COM interface (in my case, COM4) only shows up when the adapter is plugged in.
Why choose such a high COM port number? You might want to try a lower one in the device manager settings. Could you provide a screenshot?

Commenter asked: Why use a high COM port? Try a lower one in Device Manager. Can you share a screenshot? Second user responded: Unable to access IP address COM25. And another asked: What does this have to do with the IP address error? Best regards.
Hello [user_name], I'm also unsure—either there's an IP address issue or trouble selecting a COM port. That's why I requested a screenshot.

I'm frustrated; after making so many changes I lost track, but suddenly it works. Now I need to review all the settings I've modified to replicate this success next time. Thanks for everyone's suggestions.
These things sometimes happen—no worries, at least you're operational. If you don't mind sharing, what project are you working on? w

I've developed a program for a safety device that goes inline with a pump's supply cable. It features a N/O contactor, pressure and vacuum sensors, plus a PT100. If any sensor is triggered, the contactor disengages and the motor won't restart until F4 is pressed. The touchscreen displays: pump running, three faults, and "F4 to reset".
Can I upload the program here?

Thanks for sharing—it's interesting to see creative uses with [product_name]. Posting your program here might invite both helpful feedback and criticism. Are you planning to use a [product_name] operator device for this? If the environment is harsh, consider using physical buttons rather than relying on touchscreen inputs for operators. Thanks for considering this. w
I'm open to constructive feedback. When I try to upload the program, I receive an error stating 'file type not allowed.' Is there a specific method for uploading files?
I've managed to convert it to PDF, but I still can't upload the [product_name] program file.

Hello, your issue is not caused by the version of [product_name] software. It's the interface setting: your software is configured for IP address transfer, but you're using a device with COM port support. Change your upload/download settings from IP address to PC cable. To do this: 1. Go to TOOLS > OPTIONS; 2. Select the interface and choose the [product_name] cable option; 3. Confirm with OK. Then try uploading. Thanks & regards, [user_name]
The forum does not allow [product_name] files directly. To upload one, compress it into a zip file first.

Hi, if you want to upload a program file, first zip it. The forum supports only a few formats for upload. Here's a screenshot for selecting the proper settings for transferring a program from [product_name] V[version_no] to [product_name] [article_no]: select the correct module in your file, the appropriate cable, and COM port in the interface settings. Usually, you don't need to adjust baud rates. Ensure the USB cable driver is installed on your PC. Hope that helps.
A new question from [user_name] has been moved to a separate thread: "Unable to access the IP Address COM3" [product_name] V[version_no]. Best regards, Min_Moderator
Hi, I'm experiencing the same issue but can't find anything about communication under tools > options, just editing features and colors.
You won't find the interface settings in Tools > Options. That dialog appears when you use Tools > Transfer and try to send or receive a program.
Thanks, friend. That's actually what I did, and now I see the attached message.
Which cable are you using? Is it the original USB cable from [company_name]? Which operating system do you have? Please provide more details.
Using the original cable, on Windows 7 64 bit.
Which 'original' cable specifically? USB or RS232?
PC/USB cable.

I use a USB/RS232 converter in combination with the original RS232 cable for [product_name]. I connect immediately to an old [article_no]. If I disconnect the cable, I get the same error. Which [product_name] version do you have?
A new question from [user_name] is now a separate thread: 'COM port doesn't show at all in the dropdown.' Best regards, Min_Moderator

analysis.insight_summary: The main issue is difficulty uploading a program to a new [article_no] module using [product_name] V[version_no] and a USB cable, with problems including connection failures and unclear error messages referencing high COM port numbers and IP address mismatches. Users discuss potential solutions involving port assignment management, cable and adapter compatibility, and checking device manager settings. The user interface lacks clarity in its feedback, making it challenging for new users to resolve setup and communication issues.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect a straightforward and reliable process for connecting to and uploading programs with the supplied USB cable and software. They anticipate clear, actionable error messages and guidance when issues arise, particularly regarding port assignments and compatibility. New users desire intuitive feedback and solutions when problems occur.
